question: Of 8 well-supported historically extirpation-affected Azorean taxa documented on Pico in >=2 PRIBES survey years, are any positively recorded on the same exact source GPS-location proxy in more than one calendar year?

eligibility.strict_S1: Well-supported island-level extirpation, Azores, unique case taxon normalized binomial
eligibility.Pico_field: Event-core author-verified year,month,day; Occurrence extension coreid to source Event index0; exact taxonRank=species; not explicitly absent; canonical genus epithet name
eligibility.site_unit: same island and identical decimalLatitude/decimalLongitude rounded to five decimal places, not true permanent author site
eligibility.year_unit: distinct valid 2020/2021/2022/2024 original author Event calendar years
eligibility.positive_repetition: same S1 taxon at same GPS5 site in at least two different years
eligibility.sensitivity_sites: GPS4 and GPS3 separately to quantify scale dependence, never promote to primary
eligibility.do_not_use: eventID as siteID, locality string as plot, missing taxa as absence, year-to-year abundance as population persistence, source status as natal origin
eligibility.coordinate_uncertainty: report source uncertainty numeric summaries without coordinates or taxon IDs; a nominal precise coordinate does not override source uncertainty

outputs: valid original event count and dated year histogram
Pico field taxon-year n11, n8 multi-year invariants
confirmed repeated taxon×GPS site-year positives at GPS5
number of eight multi-year taxa confirmed same GPS proxy location across 2+ years
number of valid parent Event/Occurrence joins
interpretation: Positive repeated GPS proxy records are evidence of recurring source documentation, not verified identical individuals, breeding, genetic rescue or colonization. Zero GPS repetition does not mean extinct on Pico.
